title: Nvidia hardware worth $11.4M vanished between Oakland and Texas
gist: An $11.4M shipment of Nvidia hardware disappeared in transit from Oakland to Fort Worth in late August, part of a wave of increasingly professional heists that have taken more than $100M in similar shipments since June. High overseas resale premiums in export-restricted markets are cited as the driver.

insights.claim: Six pallets of Nvidia equipment worth $11.4 million vanished after leaving Oakland on August 29 on a truck bearing a food transportation company's logo bound for Fort Worth, with no arrests or recovery two months later.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Logistics and cargo security for AI hardware is a growing cost and risk in the supply chain.
insights.locator: As reported by The Mercury News

insights.claim: Thieves have stolen more than $100 million in similar tech hardware shipments since June, using techniques such as GPS location spoofing and arranging collisions with police escort vehicles.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Rising insurance, security and logistics costs for GPU shipments; opportunity for cargo-security vendors.
insights.quote: thieves have made off with more than $100 million in similar shipments since June
insights.locator: The theft in Oakland is the latest

insights.claim: In 2025, police investigated burglaries of more than $7.5 million of Nvidia hardware around Fremont and Union City, California.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Nvidia gear is a repeat target, implying persistent black-market demand.
insights.locator: Nvidia’s hardware has been a specific target

insights.claim: Stolen components can be stripped and sold in gray markets or shipped overseas to places where access to US tech hardware is restricted.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Export controls create a price premium that incentivizes theft and smuggling, undermining control effectiveness.

insights.claim: UC Berkeley's Olaf Groth says a chip costing about $550,000 can fetch $1 million or more abroad, and larger cargoes and complex heists point to professionalization of hijacking teams.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: A ~2x overseas premium quantifies the gray-market arbitrage created by restrictions and scarcity.
insights.quote: if a chip costs about $550,000, then they go for about $1 million or more abroad.

insights.claim: A September heist of two trailers marked with Nvidia and PlusAI logos yielded only 20,000 pounds of sand each, used to simulate freight for autonomous trucking tests.
insights.speaker: Nick Indge
insights.so_what: Branded trailers attract thieves, suggesting unmarked logistics as a mitigation.
